Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm
you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please tell me in your own words what happened on the day of the accident.
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Baytown, waiting to turn. The car behind me didn't stop in time and
hit me from the back. It wasn't a huge impact, but I felt it right away.
Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, I got out and walked around. The other driver said they were sorry and looked shaken up. We exchanged
information and waited for the police to come.
Q: Did you go to a doctor or an urgent care afterward?
A: I went to urgent care that same evening. They checked my neck and back and said I had a neck strain. They gave
me a prescription for a muscle relaxer and told me to rest and use ice.
Q: Are you still having symptoms?
A: Yes. My neck is stiff, especially when I turn my head to check traffic or back out of the driveway. Some mornings
the pain is worse, and I get a dull ache between my shoulders.
Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I took a few days off to rest, and I've been limiting how long I sit at my desk. I'm working, but it's been
uncomfortable.
Q: Do you currently have a follow-up appointment scheduled?
A: Yes, I have a visit with my primary care doctor next week. They're going to decide whether I need physical therapy.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident or your injuries?
A: No, I think that covers it. I'll send over the urgent care paperwork when I get home.
Q: Thank you for your time. We'll be in touch soon.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
